questions.stem: A tangent is drawn to the curve $y = x^2$ at the point $(3, 9)$. The tangent passes through $(5, 21)$. What is the gradient of the curve at $x = 3$?
questions.explanation: The gradient of the tangent is $\frac{21 - 9}{5 - 3} = \frac{12}{2} = 6$. The gradient of the curve at a point equals the gradient of the tangent at that point.

questions.stem: On a distance-time curve, the gradient of the tangent at any point gives:
questions.explanation: The gradient of a distance-time graph gives the speed. At a specific point on a curve, the tangent's gradient gives the instantaneous speed at that moment.

questions.stem: If the gradient of a curve changes from positive to zero to negative, the curve has a:
questions.explanation: When the gradient goes from positive (rising) to zero to negative (falling), the curve reaches a peak. This is a maximum turning point.
